In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the humanities are not a single discipline, but a family of different disciplines with different ways of producing and communicating research.
there are many ways of evaluating the impact of humanities research, each with their own strengths and weaknesses.

the societal impact of research in the social sciences and humanities is difficult to capture in a research evaluation system, but that the system should be designed so as to be as comprehensive as possible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evaluation systems should be more flexible and open to the diversity of research activities and impact types, and should not be based on one-size-fits-all indicators.

the humanities research community needs to be more aware of what they want from the research evaluation system, and how that can be delivered, and that the research evaluation system needs to be more reflective on how it can deliver on what the humanities community want.

we have to accept that the impact of humanities research is a complex and messy phenomenon, but that this is no reason to abandon the attempt to evaluate it, but to do so in a way that is fair to the different ways in which different research disciplines produce impact.
The main takeaway from our work is that
research evaluation systems need to be more reflective of the messiness of research impact, and more sensitive to the different kinds of impact that different kinds of research have.
the evaluation of research impact in humanities is a complex and multi-dimensional issue that cannot be solved by the use of quantitative indicators alone.
research impact is not a single thing and that it is not possible to measure it in a single way.
